newsitem.title: HUNGARY: U.S.'s Internet Tradeline comes to Hungary, CEurope.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Internet Tradeline comes to Hungary, CEurope.

text.p: U.S.-based Internet Tradeline Inc (ITI) said on Thursday it will offer small and medium-sized businesses electronic trading in Hungary and other central European countries under the Fair Business Line brand name.
"We are ready to roll this program out simultaneously in some 30 countries worldwide," Leonid Khutorsky, ITI's general manager, told a news conference.
Internet Tradeline offers an Internet site where firms can display information such as product descriptions and price lists.
Khutorsky said subscribers would be able to trade directly over the Internet.

ITI recently signed a licensing agreement with Canada's Central European Investment Company Holding Ltd. (CEIC) under which CEIC will offer ITI's service in central and eastern Europe and some countries of the former Soviet Union.

Peter Lorincze, general manager of Fair Business Line Hungary (FBLH), which is 70 percent Canadian-owned and 30 percent Hungarian, said the first 6,000 subscribers will also be given shares in FBLH to the value of the first year's subscription fee.
A one-year subscription fee for the basic service would be under 500,000 forints ($2,759).
ITI's global competitors include U.S.-based International Commerce Exchange Systems (ICES) and World Merchandise Exchange (Womex), which also offer Internet-based business-to-business services.
